    Module

    src/Connector.Core/DynamicImport

    Layer domain · project Connector.Core

    Project navigation: Connector.Core

    Overview 🤖

    Contains classes and records for handling dynamic import operations, including suggestions, evaluations, and plans.

    Responsibilities. Manages the logic for suggesting, evaluating, and building plans for dynamic import operations.

    Usage. Used by the API and infrastructure modules to handle dynamic import operations.

    AI draft from the facts on this page; review it, then write the module's documentation yourself.

    Key components

    Component Kind Used by Summary
    ImportNodeJson class 5 Deserializes an ImportNode tree stored as JSON (on ImportDefinitionEntity.RootNode), backfilling missing properties the same way ExportNodeJson does: a tree saved before a property existed must not crash every consumer that dereferences it. Every read of a persisted ImportNode tree must go through this instead of a raw Deserialize<T>` call.
    ImportPlanJson class 4 Serializes/deserializes ImportPlan for ImportRunEntity.PlanJson (Connector.Infrastructure) — a thin wrapper (matching ImportNodeJson's role for RootNode) so every read/write of that column goes through one place, even though, unlike ImportNode, ImportPlan has no recursive shape needing missing-property backfill.
    ImportPlanBuilder class 3 Reshapes an ImportWalkResult (a per-row diff tree, built for preview/review) into an ImportPlan (a flat, structured write list plus the six ImportRunEntity (Connector.Infrastructure) statistics). Pure and DB-free: everything it needs is already in the walk result. Only root-row fields become operations.ImportChildResult diffs (an object-kind child like maintenancePlan) stay visible in the walk result for the review UI, but are never turned into a write here: AllowedWritableColumns covers root-entity columns only. A child-row write path would need a stable single-row key for an object child (ImportChildResult confirms a child matched but doesn't carry the matched row's own key value out of the walker) and a per-item key for an array child, which the data model doesn't have.
    ImportNode record 2 One node in a recursive import tree — the write-side mirror of ExportNode: same shape (root/scalar-field/object/array, arbitrarily nested via Children, reusing FieldMapping verbatim for value coercion), walked in the opposite direction. Deliberately its own type rather than merged into ExportNode: SourceKey reads from inbound JSON where ExportNode.SourceField reads from SQL, TargetColumn writes to SQL where ExportNode.TargetKey writes to JSON, and OnMissingChild is a write-only policy with no export-side analogue — forcing both into one type would mean nullable fields that are meaningless half the time.
    ExportDefinitionShape record 1 The subset of a persisted ExportDefinitionEntity (Connector.Infrastructure) that SuggestFrom needs. A plain Core-level record because Connector.Core has no dependency on Connector.Infrastructure. The caller loads it from ExportLogDbContext.ExportDefinitions and deserializes RootNode via ExportNodeJson first — this type does no I/O of its own.
    ImportChildResult record 1 One Object/Array child's resolution result for one parent row: whether its JoinKey resolved to an existing related row, and — for Object children only, where "the related row" is unambiguous — the field-level diff for that row. Array children only get the existence check: no ImportDefinition writes to a child table, and matching individual array items to individual existing rows needs a per-item identity key the data model doesn't have.
    ImportFieldDiff record 1 One column-level change a walked row would make: the value currently stored in the ERP versus the (already FieldMapping-coerced) value the inbound record supplies. Only emitted when the two differ — an unchanged column contributes no entry, since "diff" means "what would actually change." OldValue is not just display data: the commit-time concurrency check uses it as the conditional write's expectedOldValue — an UPDATE guarded on the target column still matching this value — so a row whose ERP state moved on since this diff was computed is caught, not silently overwritten.
    ImportMappingCandidateField record 1 One best-effort candidate field offered alongside the deterministic root prefill — unchecked/disabled by default. The operator must explicitly enable it, and it still goes through the schema-aware AllowedWritableColumns validator before it can be saved as writable; matching a key name back to the same underlying column is a name-based heuristic, not a proven contract.

    SuggestFrom(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape>, Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape) Finds the (at most one, per the save-time uniqueness constraint) enabled export among candidates whose (IntegrationKey, ContractVersion) equals sample's pair, then builds the suggestion from it. Returns null — never throws — whenever there is nothing to suggest. Thin wrapper over Evaluate that drops the miss reason. 1
    Evaluate(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape>, Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape) Same lookup as SuggestFrom, but on a miss names which gate stopped it (ImportMappingSuggestionMiss) instead of collapsing every reason into a bare null — the API layer uses this to turn "no match found" into an operator-facing explanation (a candidate exists but is disabled, or exists but has no CorrelationKeySourceField, vs. no candidate at all). 12

    ImportMappingSuggestionMiss

    enum · ImportMappingSuggestion.cs

Ordered by how far the sample got.

    ImportPlanOperation

    record · ImportPlan.cs

    One column-level write the commit step makes: the value observed on the ERP row when the plan was built (ExpectedOldValue) and the value to write in its place. This is the same value OldValue already carries — the field is renamed here, not re-derived, to make its second job explicit: ImportRunReleaser's (Connector.Infrastructure) conditional UPDATE ... WHERE ... IS NOT DISTINCT FROM @expectedOldValue guard uses this exact value, so a row whose ERP state moved on since staging is excluded from the commit rather than silently overwritten. CorrelationValue is carried for audit/troubleshooting only — the commit itself addresses the row via Table/KeyColumn/KeyValue, which are always RootTable/RootMatchColumn/the matched root row's correlation value (see ImportPlanBuilder for why child-table writes aren't emitted here).

    Linked tests: ImportRunReleaserPostgresTests.InsertPlan, ImportRunReleaserPostgresTests.ReleaseAsync_UnrelatedFailureMidCommit_RollsBackEverythingAndMarksFailed, ImportRunReleaserPostgresTests.ReleaseAsync_UpdateOfDateAndTextColumns_ConvertsToColumnTypes, ImportRunReleaserPostgresTests.SingleOperationPlan — test code that uses it, not coverage

    ImportRowResult

    record · ImportNodeWalkResult.cs

    One inbound record's full walk result: whether its root row was matched, the field-level diff if so, and the resolution of every object/array child under it. CorrelationValue is kept even for a rejected/quarantined row (null only when the record had no readable correlation value at all) so a review UI can show which vendor record failed to match, not just a bare count.

    Linked tests: ImportPlanBuilderTests.AcceptedRow, ImportPlanBuilderTests.Build_InsertedRow_CountsAsInsertAndEmitsInsertOperations, ImportPlanBuilderTests.Build_InvalidRow_CountsSeparatelyFromRejected, ImportPlanBuilderTests.Build_MultipleRowsMixedOutcomes_CountsEachExactlyOnce, ImportPlanBuilderTests.Build_ObjectChildFieldDiff_IsNotEmittedAsAnOperation, ImportPlanBuilderTests.Build_QuarantinedRow_FoldsIntoRejectedCount, ImportPlanBuilderTests.Build_RejectedRow_CountsAsRejectedNotMatched — test code that uses it, not coverage

    ImportRowStatus

    enum · ImportNodeWalkResult.cs

    Outcome of matching one inbound record's correlation key against RootTable/ RootMatchColumn. Rejected and Quarantined both mean "excluded from the accepted set" (see UnmatchedRootPolicy) — kept distinct here so a review UI can show which policy fired, not just that the record didn't match; ImportPlanBuilder folds both into ImportRunEntity.RejectedCount, since that entity has no separate quarantine counter. Invalid is for a record that isn't even a well-formed row to evaluate a policy against (e.g. not a JSON object) — distinct from Rejected, which means the row parsed fine but its correlation key didn't match anything. Accepted covers both "matched/changed" and "matched/unchanged" — a row whose target fields already equal the incoming values is still Accepted here, just with an empty Fields diff; ImportPlanBuilder is what splits that back out into ChangedCount/ UnchangedCount.

    ImportSampleShape

    record · ImportMappingSuggestion.cs

    The inbound sample a suggestion is built from: the provenance pair read off the sample ImportEnvelope (null when the sample carries no provenance block, which yields no suggestion, never an error) and the top-level JSON key names of one sample record, used only for the best-effort candidate-field scan.

    ImportValidationException

    class · ImportNodeWalkResult.cs

    Thrown for a structural problem with the saved ImportDefinition itself (a TargetColumn outside AllowedWritableColumns, a missing root match field, malformed inbound JSON) — never for an individual record's data, which is reported via ImportRowResult instead. Distinguishing the two matters to the caller: a thrown exception means "this run cannot proceed at all," while a rejected/quarantined row is a normal, expected part of a successful walk.

    ImportWalkResult

    record · ImportNodeWalkResult.cs

    Full result of walking one inbound JSON file against one ImportNode tree: a diff-only shape for preview/review. The persisted write list (PlanJson) is built from it by ImportPlanBuilder.

    UnmatchedRootPolicy

    class · ImportNode.cs

    Discriminator values for ImportDefinitionEntity.UnmatchedRootPolicy: what happens to an inbound record whose correlation key matches no root row. Insert creates the row, and is only accepted on a definition with an IntegrationKey (a connector-to-connector contract, never a vendor file).
